# Alcántara - TV Broadcast Overlay Control System

A professional TV broadcast overlay control system built with a modern tech stack.

Alcantara also owns the versioned public-destination decision for each explicit
television Start. The command always follows Alcantara → Alana → Croccante;
only Croccante resolves stream-key-bearing Secrets Manager values. See
[`docs/broadcast-destinations.md`](docs/broadcast-destinations.md) for the
catalog, permission, immutable selection, recovery, and redaction contracts.

## Tech Stack

- **Frontend**: React Router v7 + Vite + Tailwind CSS
- **Backend**: NestJS + Fastify + Prisma
- **Database**: PostgreSQL
- **Monorepo**: pnpm workspace

- Per-song recorded intro assignment, validation, and stable sequence identity

- External renderer registration and the versioned manifest boundary are

- The proposed managed RTMP/WHIP/HLS/SRT source boundary, local measurements,

### Six-guest WebRTC contribution

The Calls console at `/calls` provides six reusable guest slots. An operator
with `alcantara:webrtc:operate` can create a persisted private invitation,
choose its one-to-seven-day lifetime (24 hours by default), copy it, replace or
revoke it, remove its current session, and select the guest's Program, Preview,
or no return video plus Program/Master, monitor, or Aux 1-8 return audio.
Invitation secrets are shown only at creation/replacement; the database stores
only their SHA-256 hash. Guest and operator LiveKit credentials expire after
five minutes and are scoped to one program room. The LiveKit API secret never
enters either browser.

Guests enter `/guest/:invitation` without Cognito, select devices, preview their
camera, test their speaker/network, and confirm headphones before explicitly
joining. A documented acoustic-risk override is available when headphones are
impossible. Each invitation permits one active browser session. A signed
session lease refreshed every 20 seconds preserves the stable slot for a
60-second network-reconnect window; a second browser fails closed. Revocation
disconnects the guest and prevents future credentials. A join refused as
revoked, expired or invalid (401 or 403) ends the guest's session; any other
refusal (the invitation in use in another window, the studio not ready, a
network or room-connection failure) keeps the preflight and lets the guest
press Join again. A refused camera or microphone permission keeps Join locked.

Operator mute is immediate. Camera/microphone enable is delivered as a request
that the guest accepts or rejects. Standby/live/wrap cues and private messages
persist requested, delivered, acknowledged/read, rejected, or failed state. A
message is marked read as soon as the guest's page shows it and stays on screen
until the guest presses Acknowledge, so operators see read and then
acknowledged.
Private talkback publishes only to the target guest's N-1 route and never to the
Program feed. Removing or disconnecting a guest does not mutate Preview or
Program.

Layouts use the `webrtc-guest` component with a generic slot number from 1-6,
not a person or invitation identifier. Assigning a replacement invitation to
the same slot therefore preserves reusable layouts. The normal Preview, CUT,
and TAKE workflow remains the only way a guest reaches air.

#### Return routing

Alana remains the owner of captured Program/Preview output publication. Start
its Program renderer with `?renderer=1` so guest microphones are excluded from
the captured base bus, and publish the output to the matching
`alcantara-<programId>` LiveKit room as `program-feed-<programId>` (and optional
`preview-feed-<programId>`). Run one isolated
`/return-router/<programId>#key=<WEBRTC_RENDERER_KEY>` renderer alongside it.
The fragment is immediately moved to session storage and removed from browser
history; it is never sent in a URL request.

The return router subscribes to the selected processed base bus, connected
guest microphones, and targeted producer talkback. It creates and publishes a
distinct Web Audio destination for every guest, excluding only that guest's
own microphone. Guests subscribe only to their selected video output and their
own `mixminus:<identity>:<bus>` track. This replaces the earlier fixed 250 ms
browser relay and keeps isolated guest tracks out of the guest UI.

Authorized operators can control Alana's independent composed-Program recorder
without treating a requested or finalizing operation as safe media. See
[`docs/program-recording.md`](docs/program-recording.md) for the pinned Alana
contract, state semantics, permissions, idempotency, local fixture, private
configuration, metrics, and recovery boundary.

#### Local and production operations

The production backend also writes a verified, encrypted logical PostgreSQL
backup to the media bucket at the top of every UTC hour. See
[`docs/production-database-backups.md`](docs/production-database-backups.md) for
the recovery boundary, storage path, telemetry, and post-deployment checks.

`docker compose up --build` includes LiveKit 1.13.4 with fixed local-only
credentials and TCP/UDP media ports. Alcantara continues to use its existing
database and Pompeii authorization configuration; this stack does not start a
second Pompeii service. From `/calls`, create six fictional guest
links and open them in separate browser contexts. Chrome's fake-device flags
may be used for repeatable automated media UAT. Verify all six show as connected
without appearing on Preview/Program, assign slots to a reusable layout, then
exercise Preview and TAKE deliberately. Restart one guest and verify its slot
is held for 60 seconds. The machine-only return router requires the local
`WEBRTC_RENDERER_KEY` from Compose.

Production owns LiveKit, Redis, TLS, TURN/TLS, firewall rules, health checks,
and secrets through Alcantara deployment infrastructure. Start from
`infra/livekit.production.example.yaml`, generate real API/session/renderer
secrets in the application-scoped secret. Route public LiveKit HTTPS/WSS through
the existing port-443 edge, and expose WebRTC TCP 7881, TURN/TLS 5349, TURN UDP
3478, and the configured UDP media/relay ranges. Validate TURN
from a restrictive external network before scheduling remote guests. Never use
the committed local credentials outside Compose. The Calls console reports the
feature as unavailable until `LIVEKIT_CONFIG_B64`, `LIVEKIT_API_KEY`,
`LIVEKIT_API_SECRET`, `WEBRTC_SESSION_SECRET`, `WEBRTC_RENDERER_KEY`, and the
public `LIVEKIT_WS_URL` deployment variable are configured; their absence does
not block unrelated Alcantara deployments.

### Radio automation

Continuous filler rotation, optional timed content blocks, per-cue browser voice tracks, output confidence, and a prepared Palazzo recovery playlist are documented in [`docs/radio-station-workflow.md`](docs/radio-station-workflow.md).

Radio song sequences default to autoplay when their mode is absent. An explicit
operator choice of Manual remains authoritative. In autoplay, Alcantara advances
to the next playlist item only after Palazzo reports that the active track ended;
looped playlists wrap to the first item and non-looped playlists stop at the end.
Shuffle persists and displays a randomized no-repeat order, advances through it
on the same authoritative Palazzo end events, and wraps only when Loop is on.
Play Next is a separate persisted FIFO queue of playlist references. It never
interrupts the current track. At the next authoritative track end it takes
priority, then Autoplay or Shuffle resumes from the playlist successor that
would have played; Manual remains stopped after the queue drains.
Up to 12 playlist songs can be starred for High Rotation. Automatic playback
opens one High Rotation opportunity every 30 minutes, chooses the least
recently played eligible favorite, and persists authoritative starts across
restarts. The 48 daily opportunities are distributed evenly across the current
favorites, guaranteeing at least four plays per favorite per day: 12 favorites
play four times each, while four favorites play 12 times each. The repeat gap
scales with the pool (`favorite count / 2` hours), avoiding repeats until every
other favorite has had its opportunity. Play Next remains the explicit
operator override, and any queued favorite play counts when choosing the least
recently played song.
The playback bar exposes pressed states for Manual, Autoplay, Shuffle, and Loop
and labels backend playback feedback as live or stale.

The Radio desk includes live Song, Audio clips / bumpers, and Main mixer
controls. Playlist rows can be starred for High Rotation or added to Play Next
without changing playlist order, and the queue supports removal and ordering
before playback. Radio
distribution at `/radio-settings` owns Palazzo automation,
bumper policy, and now-playing consumers so live playout is not mixed with
configuration. Simulcast uses the TV switcher with an explicit radio-leg status
rail. Mixer mutations are applied to Palazzo as well as persisted; bumper
configuration fields are validated and saved by the radio settings API.
All Palazzo traffic is backend-only, restricted to the private broadcast
network and approved origin, and explicitly program-scoped. The shared machine
client preserves playback/idempotency IDs across retries and is also used by
telemetry reconnect and startup recovery.
See [`docs/radio-telemetry.md`](docs/radio-telemetry.md) for the contract,
Secrets Manager bootstrap, allowlisted URLs, failure behavior, and metrics.

### Program output

Alcantara is the program control plane. A program can reference an immutable
template manifest published by Cronkite; the operator UI opens that external
renderer with the program ID and Alcantara API origin from the manifest's
runtime-parameter contract. The legacy `/program/:programId` renderer remains
only as a temporary rollback path until the Fifthbell registration and live
cutover have been verified. See
[Program template contracts](docs/program-templates.md) for registration,
security, state/SSE projection, metrics, and removal gates.

### Control Page (`/control`)

- Mode-aware Bleecker sidebar shell with desktop rail and mobile drawer
- Program/Preview switcher deck with CUT, TAKE, two-step fade-to-black, and
  Director, Audio, and Remote workspaces
- Scene staging separated from Program activation
- Real-time chyron text updates
- Type-aware TV, Radio, and Simulcast operating surfaces

The complete navigation, surface, safety, responsive, and fixture contract is in

- id, name, componentType, settings (JSON)

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Docker & Docker Compose

### AWS infrastructure ownership

Macondo provisions the shared Cumulus host, network, and Arauco database. The
service-specific AWS integration lives in [`infra/aws`](infra/aws): Alcántara
owns its GitHub OIDC deployment role, API DNS record, and the policies granting
the Cumulus host access to media storage. Macondo grants its instance
role access to every database secret it provisions; the backend resolves
Arauco credentials inside the container through that instance profile.

### Development

#### Option 1: Using Docker Compose (recommended)

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

This starts PostgreSQL, applies every committed migration non-interactively,
loads deterministic fictional data, and starts the backend, frontend, and
LiveKit. No AWS or Cognito account is needed for local development. Ports are
configurable via `.env`:

- **Backend** (NestJS, default port 3000) with hot reload via `nest start --watch`
- **Frontend** (React Router/Vite, default port 5173) with HMR
- **Broadcast destinations** (`/broadcasts`) with two fictional, version-pinned
  local catalog entries. This exercises the normal API, authorization guards,
  PostgreSQL snapshots, and Alana client boundary.
- **Alana contract fixture** on the private Compose network, used only for local
  destination reload/Start/Stop exercises. It validates authentication,
  sequencing, and exact selection acknowledgement without AWS or public output;
  it is not a deployment or a substitute for production Alana/Croccante proof.

Source directories are mounted so changes are reflected immediately.

The local stack never reaches real AWS or another real outside service
(gaulatti/alcantara#206):

- **Media store.** Uploads, song and artwork playback, radio recovery audio and
  filler digests use a localstack S3 (`localstack/localstack:4.0.3`, port
  `LOCALSTACK_PORT`, default 4566) with the bucket `alcantara-local-only`,
  created by `infra/localstack-init/01-bucket.sh`. Objects are served at
  `http://localstack.localhost:4566/alcantara-local-only/…`, which the browser
  and the backend both resolve to the host's published port.
- **Credentials.** Compose overrides every AWS name `backend/.env` could hold
  with local placeholders or empty values, does not mount `~/.aws`, and empties
  `ARAUCO_SECRET_ID`, so no Secrets Manager secret is read. The frontend gets
  empty `VITE_COGNITO_*` and `VITE_FQDN`; TEST AUTH needs none of them.
- **Start-up refusal.** Outside production the backend refuses to start when
  `MEDIA_S3_BUCKET` is set without `MEDIA_S3_ENDPOINT`, or when
  `MEDIA_S3_ENDPOINT` or `LOCAL_MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` points anywhere but a
  local host (loopback, `*.localhost` or a Compose service name). Production
  refuses to start with either of those two variables set. Each error names the
  variable, never its value.
- **Now-playing and charts.** Outside production no now-playing consumer is
  contacted (Radio settings says so, and the backend logs how many were
  skipped), and the two third-party chart feeds are not polled.
- **Check.** `scripts/check-compose-local.sh` confirms from
  `docker compose config` that every one of these names resolves to its local
  value, without printing any value.

This README is the only description of the local media store; the repository
wiki has no page for it yet.

Local browser authentication is visibly marked `TEST AUTH`. It uses short-lived
tokens with a local-only issuer and these deterministic identities:

- `operator-a` (default) and `operator-b`: normal operator permissions
- `viewer`: read-only, including denial of shared-layout publication

For visual review of the shared login shell, append `?auth-state=` to `/login`
while running the frontend in development. Supported fixtures are `loading`,
`ready`, `submitting`, `failure`, and `authenticated`; production builds ignore
the parameter. The authenticated fixture holds the visible redirect state for
inspection, while a real authenticated session continues immediately to `/`.

Choose an identity before starting or recreating the frontend:

```bash
TEST_AUTH_IDENTITY=viewer docker compose up --build
```

Re-running the backend seed restores deterministic profiles, console presets,
and TV, Radio, and Simulcast workflow fixtures without creating duplicates:

```bash
docker compose exec backend pnpm seed
```

To deliberately erase the disposable local database and replay migrations and
seed data from an empty volume:

```bash
docker compose down -v
docker compose up --build
```

The `postgres-data` volume otherwise preserves local changes across restarts.
`AUTH_MODE=test` fails startup under `NODE_ENV=production`; the issuance route
is absent when test auth is disabled, and test tokens use a distinct issuer and
audience that production verification does not accept.

The backend uses the code-owned `host.docker.internal:50087` endpoint while
developing in Compose and the code-owned `api.pompeii.gaulatti.com:443` TLS
endpoint in production with Gaulatti team `1`; no Pompeii endpoint variable is
required.
The browser attaches its current Cognito ID token to every request targeting
Alcantara's configured API origin; requests to external media and data sources
remain unchanged. A backend `401` triggers one forced Cognito session refresh;
if the refreshed request is still unauthorized, Alcantara clears the persisted
browser identity and returns the operator to login.
To populate a slideshow, upload images in the Media library and apply a label to
the required images. Order the label's assets on the Labels tab, then select the
label in the slideshow editor. Existing scenes that still reference a legacy
media group continue to render during migration.

Console preference ownership, device classification, offline behavior,
concurrency, sharing, reset, privacy, and API behavior are documented in
[Operator console preferences](docs/operator-preferences.md).

Rebuild images after dependency changes:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Run in background:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

## Identity

Alcantara authorizes through Pompeii, which now returns a canonical
`principal_id` alongside the pool subject. Operator preferences, shared console
layouts, guest invitations, and guest lifecycle audit events record it beside
the subject through nullable/additive references; ownership matches the
canonical principal when a row names one and falls back to the pool subject when
it does not, so migrated and unmigrated rows both work during rollout.

Identities are never joined by email, no ownership row changes without a verified
Pompeii mapping, and audit attribution is never rewritten. See
[`docs/canonical-principals.md`](docs/canonical-principals.md) for the inventory,
the dry-run report, and the rollback and reconciliation procedure.

The API accepts only interactive session tokens. The authorization guard
answers `401` with `{"error":"UNAUTHENTICATED","reason":"DENY_UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL"}`
for a bearer whose credential starts with `pmp_pat_` (bare or after a `Bearer`
scheme in any letter case), before any authorization call, and counts it in
`alcantara_auth_refusals_total{reason="unsupported_credential"}`. Every other
bearer is handled exactly as before.

Authorization decisions use one long-lived gRPC channel to Pompeii. A Pompeii
deploy replaces its container, and a connection through the old path can stop
carrying bytes without an error, so calls on it only time out. When an
authorization call ends in `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` or `UNAVAILABLE`, the backend
replaces the channel (each channel has its own subchannel pool, so the
replacement dials a new connection) and the next call reaches the live Pompeii.
The failed call still answers `503` with
`{"error":"AUTHORIZATION_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE"}`; nothing is allowed on a
failure. Replacements happen at most once every 5 seconds, so a Pompeii slower
than the deadline is not redialled on every request. Each replacement logs
`Pompeii channel replaced after <reason>` and counts
`alcantara_pompeii_channel_resets_total{reason="deadline_exceeded"|"unavailable"}`
(gaulatti/alcantara#225).

## Architecture

- [Access](docs/access.md) is the page where a signed-in person manages their tokens and, with `alcantara:access:manage`, the token switch and grants; [Access: backend, configuration and metrics](docs/access-api.md) documents its `/access` routes, the optional `POMPEII_ACCESS_CREDENTIAL` secret and `alcantara_access_requests_total`.
- [MCP endpoint](docs/mcp.md) documents `/mcp`, its OAuth discovery documents, who can reach it, and the registered tools.
- [External source registry](docs/external-source-registry.md) documents stable source identity, encrypted transport configuration, SSRF controls, one-time credentials, quotas, lifecycle, and metrics.

Production places the backend on the external `broadcast-control` Docker
network shared with Palazzo and Alana. Before stopping the live backend,
deployment runs
a side-effect-free runtime preflight in the new image to resolve and validate
the approved Palazzo URL and the remaining private-service configuration. The
previous container is retained until the replacement passes its startup check
and is automatically restored if the replacement fails. This keeps the existing
radio controller alive when a configuration or startup defect reaches
deployment. On the Cumulus host, deployment removes only Docker images not
referenced by any running or stopped container before pulling a release and
again after retiring the healthy predecessor. This bounds disk use without
removing the live or rollback image.

Production backend stdout and stderr remain available through `docker logs`,
using Docker's host-local `local` driver with a 10 MiB maximum per file and
three retained files. Alcantara does not require a CloudWatch Logs group or
write grant to start, restart, or roll back. See
[Production backend logging](docs/production-backend-logging.md) for validation
and rollback procedures.

The replacement joins `broadcast-control` so the private
`http://palazzo:3100` program-scoped machine API remains resolvable. Production
uses the code-owned `broadcast/production/config` Secrets Manager payload,
including Alana's private recording control URL and token and the external-source
encryption keyring. The deployment workflow validates that payload without
printing it before image build or push. During migration, deployment also
requires the running Palazzo container on the private `broadcast-control`
network. Palazzo does not require an application credential on this single-host,
single-program boundary. Preflight fails without replacing the live backend
when required configuration is unavailable or invalid.

### Data Flow

```
Control Panel → REST API → Database → SSE Broadcast → Program Page
      │                       ↓
      └── Recording API → private Alana control → composed capture state
                         Program State Update
```

1. Control page sends scene activation/chyron update via REST
2. Backend saves to database
3. Backend broadcasts update via SSE
4. Program page receives SSE event and updates display

### SSE Auto-Reconnect

The frontend SSE client automatically reconnects with a 3-second interval if the connection is lost.

Pull requests run the full verification suite and an exact 100% line/branch

# Alcantara review contract

Alcantara is a TV and radio broadcast control system. A NestJS/Fastify/Prisma
backend (PostgreSQL) owns programs, scenes, layouts, flights, the song and
instant library, radio automation driven by authoritative Palazzo playback
telemetry, LiveKit WebRTC contribution, managed external sources, versioned
broadcast-destination selection (Alcantara to Alana to Croccante) and program
recording. A React Router frontend operates it, and a small CDK package
(`infra/aws`) describes its AWS deployment role infrastructure.

Preserve program isolation, the authentication and authorization boundary,
durable idempotency before audible or public effects, bounded dependency
retries, bounded metric labels (controlled enums and normalized routes only),
and the guarantee that stream keys, signed URLs, tokens, secret payloads and
article or customer content never reach logs, metrics or responses. Command
acceptance is not proof of playout; authoritative engine observations are.
Publication and recording state are security boundaries: only an explicitly
publishable state may produce a live effect, and non-publishable states fail
closed.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance can serve this existing system without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries. Production deployment is a
separate, explicitly authorized operation: merging to `main` runs the existing
deploy workflows, and a merge is not a deployment, health or on-air claim.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new public-destination provider, a change to who may start or stop
a broadcast, a new externally exposed control surface, multi-tenant hosting, or a
change to what is retained from a recording. Ordinary implementation uncertainty
and repairable bugs belong to automated investigation, not routine human code
review. Changes to review controls, coverage scope or exclusions, or this
purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Fault injection at an
external boundary (database, network, filesystem, LiveKit, AWS) is legitimate when
the real application contract and failure handling remain exercised. The gate
requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage of the application TypeScript and
JavaScript under `backend/src` for every contribution, including external forks,
and unloaded modules are measured. The React frontend (`frontend/`), the CDK package
(`infra/aws`) and `backend/scripts` are outside the exact-coverage gate for now;
their own tests still run where they exist. Narrowing or widening the gate is a
review-control change that requires owner confirmation.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. All native tests, exact coverage and
branch protections remain mandatory. Clouseau owns the shared scoring,
investigation, repair bounds, evidence ledger, native approval and auto-merge;
this repository owns its purpose and real tests.

# MCP capabilities

Capabilities are the Alcantara console actions an MCP client reaches through
`list_capabilities` and `call_capability` (tracker: gaulatti/alcantara#210).
A capability is a `McpToolSpec` with `firstClass: false`, built by an
`@Injectable()` class decorated with `@McpToolProvider()` and listed in the
providers of the module whose services it calls. The registry finds it through
Nest discovery; appendix A of the tracker is the binding list of names,
permissions and tiers. Capabilities call the services in process with the
caller already authorized; they never call the REST API, and the four routes
whose answer is a credential are not capabilities.

Rules that hold for every capability in these files:

- The permission is the route's own, checked by the registry at call time.
- User-entered text (names, descriptions, chyron text, scene and layout
  settings, template manifests, media addresses, flight items) is moved, whole
  and unread, under an `untrusted` key beside its siblings, and the description
  ends with the untrusted-text note.
- An answer that carries a credential field (`token`, `ticket`, `secret`,
  `password`, `signature`, `credentials`, `authorization`, `apikey`) or a signed
  link (`X-Amz-Signature`, `?token=`) is withheld as `unavailable` instead of
  being returned.
- A service's own refusal is reported as the closed MCP code: 400 `invalid`,
  403 `forbidden`, 404 or "... not found" `not_found`, 409 or "... already
  exists" `conflict`; anything else stays `unavailable`.
- Metrics need nothing extra: the registry and executor count every call under
  `alcantara_mcp_requests_total{tool,tier,result}` with the registered tool
  name as the only label value.

## Program, scenes, layouts and media groups (#216)

Files: `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/{program,scenes,layouts,media-groups}.ts`,
shared helpers in `support.ts`.

### Read capabilities

| Capability | Permission | Answers like |
|---|---|---|
| `program_list_programs` | `program.read` | `GET /program` (all programs, scenes, media groups, stingers, flight sequences) |
| `program_get_staged_scene_by_id` | `program.read` | `GET /program/:programId/stage` |
| `scene_find_all` | `scene.read` | `GET /scenes` |
| `scene_find_one` | `scene.read` | `GET /scenes/:id`; a missing scene is `not_found` (REST answers an empty 200) |
| `layout_find_all` | `layout.read` | `GET /layouts` |
| `layout_find_one` | `layout.read` | `GET /layouts/:id`; a missing layout is `not_found` |
| `media_group_find_all` | `media.read` | `GET /media-groups`; `limit` is 1 to 100 (default 20), so a read is always bounded |

### Write, on-air and destructive capabilities

Every W, A and D capability has a dry run; every A and D capability has a
confirm target `{id, name}` (so the dry run returns the `confirm` string to
echo). Arguments mirror the controller's body (snake_case), and a capability
reaches the same service method with the same values: the specs call the real
controller and the capability against one set of fakes and compare the service
calls and the answers.

**Answers that are smaller than the console's.** A stored outcome is kept whole
in memory for ten minutes, so the capabilities whose route answers a whole
program, a playlist or a media group answer with ids instead (the whole
answer is one read away): the program state routes (create, rename, add and
remove scene, media group and stinger, activate, fade to black, off air) answer
`{program_id, type, active_scene_id, staged_scene_id, fade_to_black, scene_ids,
media_group_ids, stinger_ids, version}`; the scene instant routes answer the
playback without the address of the audio; `program_update_program_audio_bus_by_id`
answers the mixer settings and version without the playlist;
`media_group_create` and `media_group_update` answer the media ids without the
media rows.

**The confirm name of a program action** is the program's live stamp
(`scene:<id|null> fade:<0|1> song:<0|1> queue:<n>`), so a plan made before
something went on or off air is refused as `confirm_mismatch`. The confirm
name of a scene, layout or media group action is the target's name.

**The routes with no program id** (`/program/activate`, `/off-air`,
`/song/off-air`, `/reload`) act on the default program `main`; their
capabilities take `program_id: "main"` (the only value) so the executor spaces
on-air runs on the program. `PUT /program/broadcast-settings` is global and has
no program.

| Area | R | W | A | D | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| program (not flight, radio, recording or broadcast) | 2 | 7 | 16 | 4 | 29 |
| scenes | 2 | 2 | 4 | 1 | 9 |
| layouts | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 5 |
| media groups | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 4 |

### Step 0 of every D row: what the console does today

The console deletes in every case below, whatever is on air. The capability
refuses with `on_air` (checked again at run time, so a plan made earlier
cannot cut a live target), and its dry run says what is lost and whether it
can be recovered. The dry run of a refused target starts `REFUSED (on_air)` and
reports `onAir: true`.

| Capability | The console today | The capability |
|---|---|---|
| `program_delete_program` | Deletes the program row. The database removes its scene, media group and stinger assignments, flight sequences, radio settings and the rest by cascade, and its in-memory playback state is dropped; a program with a broadcast destination selection fails with an unexplained 500 (foreign key). It never looks at what is live. | `on_air` while a scene or fade to black is on air, a song or scene instant is playing, songs are queued or a flight sequence is active. Not recoverable. A foreign-key refusal is `conflict`. |
| `program_remove_scene_from_program` | Deletes the assignment; if the scene is on air or staged there it clears that (the picture goes blank) and stops its background audio. | `on_air` while the scene is on air, staged, or playing its background audio on that program. Recoverable (the scene returns at the end of the list). `not_found` when the scene is not assigned. |
| `program_remove_media_group_from_program` | Deletes the assignment, whatever is on air. | `on_air` while the program has a scene or fade to black on air, because its live page reads its media groups. Recoverable. |
| `program_remove_stinger_from_program` | Deletes the assignment, whatever is on air. | `on_air` while the program has a scene or fade to black on air, because its scene changes use its stingers. Recoverable. |
| `scene_remove` | Clears the scene from every program where it is on air (`scene_cleared`, the picture goes blank), deletes it and its assignments by cascade, and leaves a staged pointer to it dangling. | `on_air` while the scene is on air or staged on any program. Not recoverable (layout choice, chyron text, metadata and bracket state are gone); the dry run lists every program assignment lost. |
| `layout_remove` | Deletes the layout; the database refuses with an unexplained 500 while any scene still uses it. It never looks at what is on air. | `on_air` while a scene of the layout is on air or staged; `conflict` (a plain message) while any scene still uses it. Not recoverable. |
| `media_group_remove` | Deletes the group, its item list, its program assignments and the legacy label that mirrors it, whatever is on air; the media stay. | `on_air` while a program the group is assigned to has a scene or fade to black on air. Not recoverable (the grouping, its order and the assignments; a new group of the same media gets a new id). The dry run lists the programs it is assigned to. |

An assignment to a program that is off air is not an `on_air` case: the dry run
lists it as lost and the capability proceeds after the confirm, as the console
does.

### Other behavior worth knowing

- `program_remove_queued_program_song_by_id` is a W row (appendix A), although
  its siblings that queue and reorder are A rows; it needs `program.operate`.
- Reading a scene or layout that is not there is `not_found`; REST answers an
  empty 200.
- A W, A or D answer that would carry a credential is withheld as `unavailable`
  after the service has acted; no capability of this area returns one today.
- Metrics: the area adds no metric. Calls count under the executor's
  `alcantara_mcp_requests_total{tool,tier,result}` with the registered
  capability name, tier and a closed result as the only labels.

## Songs, media, media assets, labels and similarity (#218)

Files: `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/{songs,media,media-assets,similarity}.ts`.
`SongsMcpTools`, `MediaMcpTools` and `MediaAssetsMcpTools` are providers of
their own modules; `SimilarityMcpTools` is a provider of the radio module.

### Read capabilities

| Capability | Permission | Answers like |
|---|---|---|
| `song_find_all` | `song.read` | `GET /songs`; `limit` is 1 to 200 (default 50), where the console also accepts 0 for the whole catalog |
| `song_find_one` | `song.read` | `GET /songs/:id` (a missing song is `not_found`) |
| `media_find_all` | `media.read` | `GET /media` (limit at most 200, default 50) |
| `media_find_one` | `media.read` | `GET /media/:id` |
| `media_asset_find_all` | `access` | `GET /media-assets`, limited to the assets the caller may read |
| `media_asset_find_one` | `access` | `GET /media-assets/:id` |
| `media_asset_find_labels` | `access` | `GET /media-labels` |
| `media_asset_find_label` | `access` | `GET /media-labels/:id` |
| `radio_similarity_coverage` | `radio.read` | `GET /radio/:programId/similarity/coverage` |
| `radio_similarity_decisions` | `radio.read` | `GET /radio/:programId/similarity/decisions` (limit 1 to 200, default 50) |
| `radio_similarity_export` | `radio.manage` | `GET /radio/:programId/similarity/export`, one page of `songs` (see below) |

- Asset and label reads pass the caller's own permissions to the service, as the
  console's guard does, so a caller sees only the assets the service lets that
  caller read.
- `radio_similarity_export` answers the console's body with `songs` reduced to
  one page (`offset`, `limit`: default 200, at most 1000) and a `total` of the
  whole list, because the console's answer lists every song with its address.
- Text typed or imported by people (a song's artist, title and addresses, an
  asset's name and address, a label's name and description, a media image's name
  and address) is under `untrusted`.

### Write and destructive capabilities

Every W and D capability has a dry run; every D capability has a confirm target
`{id, name}`. There are no A rows in this area. Arguments mirror the
controller's body (snake_case) and reach the same service method with the same
values: the specs call the real controller and the capability against one set
of fakes and compare the service calls and the answers.

| Area | R | W | A | D | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| songs | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 5 |
| media | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 5 |
| media assets and labels | 4 | 5 | 0 | 2 | 11 |
| radio similarity | 3 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 4 |

- `song_create` and `song_update` take the song fields of the console's body
  (`artist`, `title`, `audio_url`, `cover_url`, `duration_ms`,
  `external_chart_id`, `external_chart_rank`, `external_chart_spins`,
  `external_chart_provider`, `enabled`, `program_id`, `intro_instant_id`); a
  field left out is not sent. `song_update` flags `onAir` in its dry run while
  a program is playing the song.
- The label writes (`media_asset_create_label`, `media_asset_update_label`,
  `media_asset_replace_label_assets`) answer the label's ids, text, times,
  `assetCount` and `assetIds`, not every asset (a stored outcome is kept whole
  in memory); `media_asset_find_label` lists the assets.
- `radio_similarity_upload` takes `program_id` (the route's, which the service
  does not read) and `upload`, the console's body; the service validates it and
  answers per song.
- **Permissions of the media asset and label writes.** The seven writes of the
  media-assets area need `media.manage`; a caller without it does not see them.
  The service then decides from the caller's own permissions: a background audio
  needs `scene.manage`, a label write any manage permission, an asset write the
  manage permission of its kind.
- **Stricter than the console.** The four D capabilities (`song_remove`,
  `media_remove`, `media_asset_remove_standalone_asset`,
  `media_asset_remove_label`) refuse with `on_air` where the console deletes,
  and `song_remove` also refuses a song that is in any program's rotation; each
  description says so.

### Step 0 of every D row: what the console does today

| Capability | The console today | The capability |
|---|---|---|
| `song_remove` | Checks the song exists, then deletes it, its media asset and cover link, its chart identity, intro assignment and embeddings in one transaction. It never looks at what is playing, queued or in a song sequence. | `on_air` while a program is playing the song, has it in its Play Next queue (a sequence item or a catalog entry) or lists it in its song sequence. Not recoverable (a new song gets a new id and must be analysed and embedded again; the file stays in storage). |
| `media_remove` | Checks the image exists, deletes it and its media asset, removes it from every media group that holds it (renumbering their items and refreshing the legacy slideshow label). Never looks at what is on air. | `on_air` while a program that reads a group holding the image has a scene or fade to black on air, or a scene on air or staged names the image address in its settings. Not recoverable. The dry run lists the programs that read it. |
| `media_asset_remove_standalone_asset` | Deletes an asset the caller may manage that is not an image, clip, song, cover or transition (the service answers 400 for those); its label assignments go by cascade. Never looks at what is on air. | `on_air` while a scene on air or staged names the asset id or address in its settings. Not recoverable. The dry run lists its label assignments and the programs with a scene that names it. |
| `media_asset_remove_label` | Deletes the label and its assignments (the assets stay); a legacy slideshow label deletes the media group it mirrors, with its program assignments. Never looks at what is on air. | `on_air` while a scene on air or staged names the label id, or a program that reads the mirrored group has a scene or fade to black on air. Not recoverable. |

An assignment to a program that is off air is not an `on_air` case: the dry run
lists it as lost and the capability proceeds after the confirm.

### Import media by URL (`import_media_from_url`)

File: `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/media-import.ts`; the work is
`UploadsService.importFromUrl`. A W capability with `upload.create`, taking
`url` (at most 2000 characters) and `kind` (`instant`, `background`, `song`,
`artwork` or `stinger`: the five kinds the console's upload routes take; #226
added the last two).

- **It covers the five `upload_*` rows.** Appendix A's `upload_instant`,
  `upload_background`, `upload_song`, `upload_artwork` and `upload_stinger` are
  multipart routes that an MCP client cannot use; they are marked
  `covered by import_media_from_url` in the tsv and are not capabilities of
  their own. The console has no import route: its uploads are multipart bodies.
  The ticket names this capability beside the rows, so the registry subset test
  pins it as an extra capability (permission `upload.create`, tier W).
- **The fetch is the outbound-request policy's** (`docs/outbound-requests.md`):
  https only, public addresses only, every redirect (at most 3) checked again,
  the content type and byte cap of the kind, streamed under the cap, one 120
  second deadline. No request header is sent. Per kind: `instant`, `background`
  and `song` take an `audio/*` type (or `application/ogg`), at most 200 MiB;
  `artwork` an avif, gif, jpeg, png or webp image, at most 10 MiB; `stinger`
  `video/webm`, at most 50 MiB (the limits of `UploadsService`'s upload
  routes). The bytes then go through `UploadsService.upload()`, so size, type
  and extension are validated as for a file the operator sends, and a song's
  tags and cover are read. An address whose answer is of another kind's type
  (an image for a song, audio for artwork) is refused before the body is read.
- **No media asset, no analysis scheduling.** An upload only stores the file
  (S3) and answers `{key, url, bucket, contentType, sizeBytes, metadata?}`; the
  asset is created by the create that follows (`song_create` or the instant and
  background creates) and analysis follows from the asset. The import does the
  same: use the answer's `url` there.
- **The address is never logged or echoed; only its file name is kept.** The
  stored object key carries the sanitised last path segment as the file name of
  a sent file does, nothing else of the address. The audit target is
  `import-<kind>`; the dry run and the answer carry no address; a refusal is
  the policy's plain message (400 as `invalid`; 502 and 504 and a failed store
  as `unavailable`). The idempotency record keeps a hash of the arguments.
- **Metric:** `alcantara_outbound_fetch_total{path="media_import",result}`,
  the policy's counter (all series start at zero); no new metric.

## Flight sequences, the rundown (#215)

File: `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/flight.ts` (`FlightMcpTools`, listed in
`ProgramModule` beside `ProgramMcpTools`), the program routes under
`/program/:programId/flight`: 14 rows of appendix A (2 R, 5 W, 6 A, 1 D), each
calling the `FlightService` method its controller calls, in process. The
closing test is `flight-appendix.spec.ts`: it reads those rows from
`appendix-a.tsv` and asserts a capability with that name, permission and tier
for each, and that the permission is the one the controller handler requires.
Sequence names, cues (`items`) and the filler warnings (which carry song
titles) are user text and sit under `untrusted`.

### Read capabilities

| Capability | Permission | Answers like |
|---|---|---|
| `program_list_flight_sequences_by_id` | `flight.read` | `GET /program/:programId/flight` (every sequence with its cues, schedule, publication state, revision and `isRunning`) |
| `program_preflight_flight_sequence_by_id` | `flight.read` | `GET /program/:programId/flight/:sequenceId/preflight` (`ready` and the `issues` found; a sequence with no scheduled start is `invalid`) |

### Write capabilities (`flight.manage`)

Arguments mirror the controller's body in snake_case (`scheduled_at`,
`sequence_id`, `program_id`); the cues and the nested `rules` keep the console's
own keys (`labelId`, `clockOffsetSeconds`, `artistSeparation`), because the
service reads them as they are. The service validates every cue, the schedule
and the revision; its refusals come back as the closed MCP codes (400 `invalid`,
404 `not_found`, 409 `conflict`). `items` is bounded at 500 cues by the
capability (a clocked log holds at most 120). `revision` is required on
`generate`, `fill` and `publish` (the service refuses any other value) and
optional on `update` (a clocked log needs it).

| Capability | Plan (dry run) |
|---|---|
| `program_create_flight_sequence_by_id` | Creates a draft; it is not active and does not air until activated and started (or published and its start arrives). Recoverable: delete it. |
| `program_update_flight_sequence_by_id` | Lists what changes, from the sequence as it is now. On a running sequence the dry run reports `onAir: true` (later cues change at once; the console refuses schedule and loop changes and edits of the cue on air or already played). The previous values are not kept. |
| `program_generate_tagged_log` | A proposal: returns the cues and saves nothing (save them with update). Refused by the console unless the log is an unaired, unpublished draft of a program with a radio leg. |
| `program_fill_rundown` | The same for the gaps of a rundown; answers cues and warnings. |
| `program_publish_flight_sequence_by_id` | Publishes a clocked log: the console then starts it by itself at its scheduled time, with nobody present, and its start cannot move. There is no unpublish (the way back is a delete, refused while it is queued, or editing its cues). Not recoverable. |

### On-air capabilities (`flight.operate`)

All six are A rows on a program (`program_id`), confirmed by the program's live
stamp with the flight position appended:
`scene:<id|null> fade:<0|1> song:<0|1> queue:<n> flight:<active id|none> running:<0|1> cue:<active cue id|none>`.
A plan made before the program went on or off air, the flight started or
stopped, or the log moved to another cue is refused as `confirm_mismatch`; for
`go` that includes the log advancing on its own timer.

| Capability | The console does |
|---|---|
| `program_activate_flight_sequence_by_id` | Makes the sequence active. A running flight stops and the song playing is cut (a sequence that is not clocked always does this, even when nothing runs); nothing starts yet. A clocked log must be published and pass preflight. |
| `program_deactivate_flight_sequence_by_id` | Stops the flight, cuts the song and clears the active sequence. |
| `program_start_flight_by_id` | Starts the active sequence from cue 1 (a running one stops, cutting the song, and starts over); its cues then act on air by themselves. |
| `program_stop_flight_by_id` | Stops the cues and cuts the song, turning the rotation to manual; the sequence stays active. |
| `program_go_flight_by_id` | Runs the next cue at once; with no flight running it starts the active sequence. A clocked log cannot advance before its scheduled start. |
| `program_reset_flight_by_id` | Stops, cuts the song, clears the position; restarts from cue 1 if it was running. |

The answers are the console's (`{activeSequenceId}` or `{ok: true}`).

### Step 0 of the D row: what the console does today

| Capability | The console today | The capability |
|---|---|---|
| `program_delete_flight_sequence_by_id` | Deletes the sequence whatever its state. A running sequence is stopped first (the song playing is cut and the rotation turns manual); if it is the active sequence the program's active pointer is cleared; a published clocked log still waiting for its start is dropped and never airs. It never looks at the as-run state. | `on_air` while the sequence is running, is the program's active sequence, or is published and queued to start (published, never started, scheduled start not more than 5 s in the past, which is the console's own start window). Checked again at run time. Not recoverable: the cues, their order, the schedule and the published state are gone, with no copy and no unpublish; the dry run lists the sequence and program and says to read it first and recreate it by hand. A sequence that is a draft, already aired, or whose start was missed is deleted after the confirm. Confirm target `{id: "<program>/<sequence>", name: <sequence name>}`. |

Metrics: the area adds none; calls count under the executor's
`alcantara_mcp_requests_total{tool,tier,result}`. `generate`, `fill` and
`publish` keep recording the console's own `radio log` results, since they call
the same service methods.

## Instants and stingers (gaulatti/alcantara#217)

Files: `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/instants.ts` (`InstantsMcpTools`, registered
in `InstantsModule`) and `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/stingers.ts`
(`StingersMcpTools`, registered in `StingersModule`). Ten appendix A rows: two
R, four W, two A and two D. All are `firstClass: false`, call the service the
console's controller calls in process (`ProgramService` for instants,
`StingersService` for stingers) and answer what the controller answers, with
user text under `untrusted`. The program and radio rows that name instants and
stingers (`program_take_program_scene_instant_by_id`,
`program_add_stinger_to_program`, `radio_play_instant` and the like) belong to
the program and radio areas, not to this one.

### Reads

- `instant_list_instants` (`instant.read`): `program_id` (optional; the console's
  `programId` query, default `main`) selects which song each instant introduces
  (`assignedSongId`). The answer is the console's list: every instant in order
  with `availableForSongIntro`. The name (and, as untrusted, the audio address)
  sit under `untrusted`.
- `stinger_list_stingers` (`stinger.read`): no arguments; every stinger, newest
  change first. Name and video address sit under `untrusted`.
- No answer carries a credential: an answer that holds a signed link or a
  credential field is withheld (`unavailable`), the same tripwire as every other
  capability, tested with a planted secret.

### Writes and operations

The service of every row is the controller's; an argument is the controller's
field in snake case, `*_id` named after the path parameter. Answers equal the
controller's answer for the same input (one set of fake services behind both),
except that user text is under `untrusted`. A service refusal is reported as the
closed MCP code (400 as `invalid`, 404 as `not_found`).

| Capability | Tier | Permission | Arguments | Answer and notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instant_create_instant` | W | `instant.manage` | `name`, `audio_url`, `volume`, `enabled` | The created instant. The service clamps `volume` to 0..1 (the console accepts any finite number, so does this); the instant goes to the end of the list and gets its media asset. |
| `instant_update_instant` | W | `instant.manage` | `instant_id`, `name`, `audio_url`, `volume`, `enabled` | The instant. A field left out stays. caller's own `Authorization` header to Pompeii's `ApplicationAccessService`
through `AccessService` with `via_client: mcp`, so Pompeii's audit shows the
change came from an MCP client. Pompeii makes every decision; Alcantara adds
no check but the `alcantara:access` permission every signed-in caller holds, and
the registry asks Pompeii again before each A and D action (`reauthorize`), so a
revoked session or a removed manage key is refused on the next call.

| Capability | Tier | Route it mirrors | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_my_tokens` | R | `GET /access/tokens` | id, name, permissions, created and last used (when and in which application). Never a value or a display prefix. |
| `revoke_my_token` | W | `DELETE /access/tokens/:id` | Dry run, no confirm. Revokes the caller's own token only (Pompeii enforces it). |
| `get_token_switch` | R | `GET /access/token-switch` | |
| `set_token_switch` | A | `PUT /access/token-switch` | Needs `alcantara:access:manage` in Pompeii. Confirm string `token switch on to off` (the switch as read now), so a plan made before someone else flipped it is refused as `confirm_mismatch`. |
| `list_access_roles` | R | `GET /access/roles` | |
| `list_grants` | R | `GET /access/grants` | |
| `grant_role` | D | `POST /access/grants` | Args `user_id`, `role_id`. Confirm names the role and user ids. Pompeii bounds it: the caller must hold every permission the role carries. |

`POST /access/tokens` is **excluded** (it returns a token value), and
`GET /access/my-permissions` is **covered by `whoami`** (the caller's own
permissions). There is no capability that creates a token, and none returns a
token value or `display_prefix`: `list_my_tokens` lists tokens through an
explicit field list, and `display_prefix` joins the keys the answer tripwire
(`assertNoCredential`) refuses, so an answer that ever carried one would be
withheld. What people typed (`name`, `user_email`, `actor_email`, `target`,
`role_name`) travels under `untrusted`.

Pompeii's errors become the closed MCP codes without its message:
`UNAUTHENTICATED` and `PERMISSION_DENIED` are `forbidden` (a personal access
token is refused as the person: sign in to manage access), `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is
`invalid`, `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (the token switch is off) is `conflict`,
`NOT_FOUND` is `not_found`, and anything else, or no service credential, is
`unavailable`. The capabilities need the connection's own credential, so an
MCP client signed in with a personal access token gets `forbidden` from Pompeii;
use an OAuth session.

`alcantara_access_request_duration_seconds{route}` count the Pompeii calls
([Access](access-api.md)); the executor counts each tool call as usual.

# MCP capabilities

Capabilities are the Alcantara console actions an MCP client reaches through
`list_capabilities` and `call_capability` (tracker: gaulatti/alcantara#210).
A capability is a `McpToolSpec` with `firstClass: false`, built by an
`@Injectable()` class decorated with `@McpToolProvider()` and listed in the
providers of the module whose services it calls. The registry finds it through
Nest discovery; appendix A of the tracker is the binding list of names,
permissions and tiers. Capabilities call the services in process with the
caller already authorized; they never call the REST API, and the four routes
whose answer is a credential are not capabilities.

Rules that hold for every capability in these files:

- The permission is the route's own, checked by the registry at call time.
- User-entered text (names, descriptions, chyron text, scene and layout
  settings, template manifests, media addresses, flight items) is moved, whole
  and unread, under an `untrusted` key beside its siblings, and the description
  ends with the untrusted-text note.
- An answer that carries a credential field (`token`, `ticket`, `secret`,
  `password`, `signature`, `credentials`, `authorization`, `apikey`) or a signed
  link (`X-Amz-Signature`, `?token=`) is withheld as `unavailable` instead of
  being returned.
- A service's own refusal is reported as the closed MCP code: 400 `invalid`,
  403 `forbidden`, 404 or "... not found" `not_found`, 409 or "... already
  exists" `conflict`; anything else stays `unavailable`.
- Metrics need nothing extra: the registry and executor count every call under
  `alcantara_mcp_requests_total{tool,tier,result}` with the registered tool
  name as the only label value.

## Program, scenes, layouts and media groups (#216)

Files: `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/{program,scenes,layouts,media-groups}.ts`,
shared helpers in `support.ts`.

### Read capabilities

| Capability | Permission | Answers like |
|---|---|---|
| `program_list_programs` | `program.read` | `GET /program` (all programs, scenes, media groups, stingers, flight sequences) |
| `program_get_staged_scene_by_id` | `program.read` | `GET /program/:programId/stage` |

| `layout_find_one` | `layout.read` | `GET /layouts/:id`; a missing layout is `not_found` |
| `media_group_find_all` | `media.read` | `GET /media-groups`; `limit` is 1 to 100 (default 20), so a read is always bounded |

### Write, on-air and destructive capabilities

Every W, A and D capability has a dry run; every A and D capability has a
confirm target `{id, name}` (so the dry run returns the `confirm` string to
echo). Arguments mirror the controller's body (snake_case), and a capability
reaches the same service method with the same values: the specs call the real
controller and the capability against one set of fakes and compare the service
calls and the answers.

**Answers that are smaller than the console's.** A stored outcome is kept whole
in memory for ten minutes, so the capabilities whose route answers a whole
program, a playlist or a media group answer with ids instead (the whole
answer is one read away): the program state routes (create, rename, add and
remove scene, media group and stinger, activate, fade to black, off air) answer
`{program_id, type, active_scene_id, staged_scene_id, fade_to_black, scene_ids,
media_group_ids, stinger_ids, version}`; the scene instant routes answer the
playback without the address of the audio; `program_update_program_audio_bus_by_id`
answers the mixer settings and version without the playlist;
`media_group_create` and `media_group_update` answer the media ids without the
media rows.

**The confirm name of a program action** is the program's live stamp
(`scene:<id|null> fade:<0|1> song:<0|1> queue:<n>`), so a plan made before
something went on or off air is refused as `confirm_mismatch`. The confirm
name of a scene, layout or media group action is the target's name.

**The routes with no program id** (`/program/activate`, `/off-air`,
`/song/off-air`, `/reload`) act on the default program `main`; their
capabilities take `program_id: "main"` (the only value) so the executor spaces
on-air runs on the program. `PUT /program/broadcast-settings` is global and has
no program.

| Area | R | W | A | D | Total |

| program (not flight, radio, recording or broadcast) | 2 | 7 | 16 | 4 | 29 |
| scenes | 2 | 2 | 4 | 1 | 9 |
| layouts | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 5 |
| media groups | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 4 |

### Step 0 of every D row: what the console does today

The console deletes in every case below, whatever is on air. The capability
refuses with `on_air` (checked again at run time, so a plan made earlier
cannot cut a live target), and its dry run says what is lost and whether it
can be recovered. The dry run of a refused target starts `REFUSED (on_air)` and
reports `onAir: true`.

| Capability | The console today | The capability |
|---|---|---|
| `program_delete_program` | Deletes the program row. The database removes its scene, media group and stinger assignments, flight sequences, radio settings and the rest by cascade, and its in-memory playback state is dropped; a program with a broadcast destination selection fails with an unexplained 500 (foreign key). It never looks at what is live. | `on_air` while a scene or fade to black is on air, a song or scene instant is playing, songs are queued or a flight sequence is active. Not recoverable. Recoverable (the scene returns at the end of the list). `not_found` when the scene is not assigned. |
| `program_remove_media_group_from_program` | Deletes the assignment, whatever is on air. | `on_air` while the program has a scene or fade to black on air, because its live page reads its media groups. Recoverable. |
| `program_remove_stinger_from_program` | Deletes the assignment, whatever is on air. | `on_air` while the program has a scene or fade to black on air, because its scene changes use its stingers. Recoverable. |
| `scene_remove` | Clears the scene from every program where it is on air (`scene_cleared`, the picture goes blank), deletes it and its assignments by cascade, and leaves a staged pointer to it dangling. | `on_air` while the scene is on air or staged on any program. Not recoverable (layout choice, chyron text, metadata and bracket state are gone); the dry run lists every program assignment lost. |
| `layout_remove` | Deletes the layout; the database refuses with an unexplained 500 while any scene still uses it. It never looks at what is on air. | `on_air` while a scene of the layout is on air or staged; `conflict` (a plain message) while any scene still uses it. Not recoverable. |
| `media_group_remove` | Deletes the group, its item list, its program assignments and the legacy label that mirrors it, whatever is on air; the media stay. | `on_air` while a program the group is assigned to has a scene or fade to black on air. Not recoverable (the grouping, its order and the assignments; a new group of the same media gets a new id). The dry run lists the programs it is assigned to. |

An assignment to a program that is off air is not an `on_air` case: the dry run
lists it as lost and the capability proceeds after the confirm, as the console
does.

### Other behavior worth knowing

- `program_remove_queued_program_song_by_id` is a W row (appendix A), although
  its siblings that queue and reorder are A rows; it needs `program.operate`.
- Reading a scene or layout that is not there is `not_found`; REST answers an
  empty 200.
- A W, A or D answer that would carry a credential is withheld as `unavailable`
  after the service has acted; no capability of this area returns one today.
- Metrics: the area adds no metric. Calls count under the executor's
  `alcantara_mcp_requests_total{tool,tier,result}` with the registered

`UploadsService.importFromUrl`. A W capability with `upload.create`, taking

  multipart routes that an MCP client cannot use; they are marked
  `covered by import_media_from_url` in the tsv and are not capabilities of
  their own. The console has no import route: its uploads are multipart bodies.

  pins it as an extra capability (permission `upload.create`, tier W).

  https only, public addresses only, every redirect (at most 3) checked again,
  the content type and byte cap of the kind, streamed under the cap, one 120
  second deadline. No request header is sent. Per kind: `instant`, `background`
  and `song` take an `audio/*` type (or `application/ogg`), at most 200 MiB;

  `video/webm`, at most 50 MiB (the limits of `UploadsService`'s upload
  routes). The bytes then go through `UploadsService.upload()`, so size, type

  background creates) and analysis follows from the asset. The import does the
  same: use the answer's `url` there.

  `import-<kind>`; the dry run and the answer carry no address; a refusal is
  the policy's plain message (400 as `invalid`; 502 and 504 and a failed store

- `destination_retire_destination`, `destination_restore_destination` and
  the other catalog rows are W: a running broadcast keeps the immutable

- Metrics: the area adds no metric. The executor counts every call under

## Access (gaulatti/alcantara#224)

File: `backend/src/mcp/capabilities/access.ts` (`AccessMcpTools`), registered in
`AccessModule` beside the `/access` controller. Each capability forwards the
caller's own `Authorization` header to Pompeii's `ApplicationAccessService`
through `AccessService` with `via_client: mcp`, so Pompeii's audit shows the
change came from an MCP client. Pompeii makes every decision; Alcantara adds
no check but the `alcantara:access` permission every signed-in caller holds, and
the registry asks Pompeii again before each A and D action (`reauthorize`), so a
revoked session or a removed manage key is refused on the next call.

| Capability | Tier | Route it mirrors | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_my_tokens` | R | `GET /access/tokens` | id, name, permissions, created and last used (when and in which application). Never a value or a display prefix. |
| `revoke_my_token` | W | `DELETE /access/tokens/:id` | Dry run, no confirm. Revokes the caller's own token only (Pompeii enforces it). |
| `get_token_switch` | R | `GET /access/token-switch` | |
| `set_token_switch` | A | `PUT /access/token-switch` | Needs `alcantara:access:manage` in Pompeii. Confirm string `token switch on to off` (the switch as read now), so a plan made before someone else flipped it is refused as `confirm_mismatch`. |
| `list_access_roles` | R | `GET /access/roles` | |
| `list_grants` | R | `GET /access/grants` | |
| `grant_role` | D | `POST /access/grants` | Args `user_id`, `role_id`. Confirm names the role and user ids. Pompeii bounds it: the caller must hold every permission the role carries. |
| `revoke_role` | D | `DELETE /access/grants/:id` | Arg `grant_id` (from `list_grants`); a grant that is not listed is `not_found`. |
| `list_access_history` | R | `GET /access/history` | Args `limit` (1 to 200) and `before` (RFC 3339). |

`POST /access/tokens` is **excluded** (it returns a token value), and
`GET /access/my-permissions` is **covered by `whoami`** (the caller's own
permissions). There is no capability that creates a token, and none returns a
token value or `display_prefix`: `list_my_tokens` lists tokens through an
explicit field list, and `display_prefix` joins the keys the answer tripwire
(`assertNoCredential`) refuses, so an answer that ever carried one would be
withheld. What people typed (`name`, `user_email`, `actor_email`, `target`,
`role_name`) travels under `untrusted`.

Pompeii's errors become the closed MCP codes without its message:
`UNAUTHENTICATED` and `PERMISSION_DENIED` are `forbidden` (a personal access
token is refused as the person: sign in to manage access), `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is
`invalid`, `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (the token switch is off) is `conflict`,
`NOT_FOUND` is `not_found`, and anything else, or no service credential, is
`unavailable`. The capabilities need the connection's own credential, so an
MCP client signed in with a personal access token gets `forbidden` from Pompeii;
use an OAuth session.

Tests: `access.registry.spec.ts` runs the nine on the registry's real call path
over the real `AccessService` (tiers, confirm, re-authorization before every A
and D, the error mapping, and a check over every answer that no token value or
display prefix is returned). `mcp.registry.appendix.spec.ts` pins the new totals.
Metrics: `alcantara_access_requests_total{route,result}` and
`alcantara_access_request_duration_seconds{route}` count the Pompeii calls
([Access](access-api.md)); the executor counts each tool call as usual.

claims.description:
Issue gaulatti/alcantara#300 (backend, read-only MCP parity, #291): two read-only capabilities on the radio read permission, same tier as the existing radio reads.

- radio_get_playback_state(program_id): the song on air (playback_request_id, elapsed_ms, duration_ms, progress, intro_status, telemetry_stale, untrusted title and artist), the next song (playback_id, status, untrusted title and artist), the rotation mode and the frozen flag; on_air is null when nothing plays.

report.summary: Adds two read-tier MCP capabilities on alcantara:radio:read (issue #300): radio_get_playback_state maps SongExecutionEngine.getOnAirView and getPlaybackState into an on_air/next/mode/frozen answer without the playback token or audio URL, and radio_get_audio_levels maps ProgramService.getProgramAudioMeter channels to vu/peak/peak_hold with updated_at. Both go through readSpec (tier R, untrusted note, credential tripwire). The registry spec lists them as extra capabilities, the appendix A broadcast spec excludes them from its route-only rows, and the capability docs table describes both. # Alcántara - TV Broadcast Overlay Control System

A professional TV broadcast overlay control system built with a modern tech stack.

Alcantara also owns the versioned public-destination decision for each explicit
television Start. The command always follows Alcantara → Alana → Croccante;
only Croccante resolves stream-key-bearing Secrets Manager values. See
[`docs/broadcast-destinations.md`](docs/broadcast-destinations.md) for the
catalog, permission, immutable selection, recovery, and redaction contracts.

## Tech Stack

- **Frontend**: React Router v7 + Vite + Tailwind CSS
- **Backend**: NestJS + Fastify + Prisma
- **Database**: PostgreSQL
- **Monorepo**: pnpm workspace

# Alcantara review contract

Alcantara is a TV and radio broadcast control system. A NestJS/Fastify/Prisma
backend (PostgreSQL) owns programs, scenes, layouts, flights, the song and
instant library, radio automation driven by authoritative Palazzo playback
telemetry, LiveKit WebRTC contribution, managed external sources, versioned
broadcast-destination selection (Alcantara to Alana to Croccante) and program
recording. A React Router frontend operates it, and a small CDK package
(`infra/aws`) describes its AWS deployment role infrastructure.

Preserve program isolation, the authentication and authorization boundary,
durable idempotency before audible or public effects, bounded dependency
retries, bounded metric labels (controlled enums and normalized routes only),
and the guarantee that stream keys, signed URLs, tokens, secret payloads and
article or customer content never reach logs, metrics or responses. Command
acceptance is not proof of playout; authoritative engine observations are.
Publication and recording state are security boundaries: only an explicitly
publishable state may produce a live effect, and non-publishable states fail
closed.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance can serve this existing system without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries. Production deployment is a
separate, explicitly authorized operation: merging to `main` runs the existing
deploy workflows, and a merge is not a deployment, health or on-air claim.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new public-destination provider, a change to who may start or stop
a broadcast, a new externally exposed control surface, multi-tenant hosting, or a
change to what is retained from a recording. Ordinary implementation uncertainty
and repairable bugs belong to automated investigation, not routine human code
review. Changes to review controls, coverage scope or exclusions, or this
purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Fault injection at an
external boundary (database, network, filesystem, LiveKit, AWS) is legitimate when
the real application contract and failure handling remain exercised. The gate
requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage of the application TypeScript and
JavaScript under `backend/src` for every contribution, including external forks,
and unloaded modules are measured. The React frontend (`frontend/`), the CDK package
(`infra/aws`) and `backend/scripts` are outside the exact-coverage gate for now;
their own tests still run where they exist. Narrowing or widening the gate is a
review-control change that requires owner confirmation.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. All native tests, exact coverage and
branch protections remain mandatory. Clouseau owns the shared scoring,
investigation, repair bounds, evidence ledger, native approval and auto-merge;
this repository owns its purpose and real tests.

The API accepts only interactive session tokens. The authorization guard
answers `401` with `{"error":"UNAUTHENTICATED","reason":"DENY_UNSUPPORTED_CREDENTIAL"}`
for a bearer whose credential starts with `pmp_pat_` (bare or after a `Bearer`
scheme in any letter case), before any authorization call, and counts it in
`alcantara_auth_refusals_total{reason="unsupported_credential"}`. Every other
bearer is handled exactly as before.

Authorization decisions use one long-lived gRPC channel to Pompeii. A Pompeii
deploy replaces its container, and a connection through the old path can stop
carrying bytes without an error, so calls on it only time out. When an
authorization call ends in `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` or `UNAVAILABLE`, the backend
replaces the channel (each channel has its own subchannel pool, so the
replacement dials a new connection) and the next call reaches the live Pompeii.
The failed call still answers `503` with
`{"error":"AUTHORIZATION_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE"}`; nothing is allowed on a
failure. Replacements happen at most once every 5 seconds, so a Pompeii slower
than the deadline is not redialled on every request. Each replacement logs
`Pompeii channel replaced after <reason>` and counts
`alcantara_pompeii_channel_resets_total{reason="deadline_exceeded"|"unavailable"}`
(gaulatti/alcantara#225).

# Alcantara review contract

Alcantara is a TV and radio broadcast control system. A NestJS/Fastify/Prisma
backend (PostgreSQL) owns programs, scenes, layouts, flights, the song and
instant library, radio automation driven by authoritative Palazzo playback
telemetry, LiveKit WebRTC contribution, managed external sources, versioned
broadcast-destination selection (Alcantara to Alana to Croccante) and program
recording. A React Router frontend operates it, and a small CDK package
(`infra/aws`) describes its AWS deployment role infrastructure.

Preserve program isolation, the authentication and authorization boundary,
durable idempotency before audible or public effects, bounded dependency
retries, bounded metric labels (controlled enums and normalized routes only),
and the guarantee that stream keys, signed URLs, tokens, secret payloads and
article or customer content never reach logs, metrics or responses. Command
acceptance is not proof of playout; authoritative engine observations are.
Publication and recording state are security boundaries: only an explicitly
publishable state may produce a live effect, and non-publishable states fail
closed.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance can serve this existing system without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries. Production deployment is a
separate, explicitly authorized operation: merging to `main` runs the existing
deploy workflows, and a merge is not a deployment, health or on-air claim.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new public-destination provider, a change to who may start or stop
a broadcast, a new externally exposed control surface, multi-tenant hosting, or a
change to what is retained from a recording. Ordinary implementation uncertainty
and repairable bugs belong to automated investigation, not routine human code
review. Changes to review controls, coverage scope or exclusions, or this
purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.
